terms: Concept generation
Brainstorming, SCAMPER, mood boards and morphological charts produce divergent ideas; convergence selects strongest concept.
Design cycle stages
IBDP DT uses analysing, designing, planning, creating, evaluating; iterative loops repeat as understanding develops.
Double Diamond model
UK Design Council 2005 process: discover and define (problem), develop and deliver (solution); two divergent-convergent diamonds.
Inquiry and analysis
Identifies user needs through observation, interviews and PMI charts; benchmarks against existing solutions.
Prototyping iteration
Low-fidelity (paper, foam, cardboard) progresses through mid-fidelity (3D-printed) to high-fidelity working models; feedback drives refinement.
Specification document
Quantitative and qualitative criteria covering function, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials, cost, sustainability; agreed before design.

Anthropometric data
Statistical measurements of body dimensions; design typically accommodates 5th-95th percentile range; Henry Dreyfuss Designing for People 1955 set standards.
Cognitive ergonomics
Donald Norman's Design of Everyday Things 1988 covers affordances, signifiers, mappings, feedback; reduces user error through mental models.
Ergonomics scope
Discipline studying human-product interaction; HFES founded 1957; IEA 1959; covers physical, cognitive and organisational dimensions.
Fitts' Law 1954
Time to acquire target = a + b log2 (D/W + 1); models pointing tasks; informs touchscreen target sizing.
Reach envelope
Three-dimensional space accessible from a posture; primary, secondary and tertiary zones inform car cockpit and kitchen layouts.
Static vs dynamic anthropometrics
Static measures stationary body; dynamic captures reach, range of motion and clearance during movement.

Cradle to cradle
William McDonough and Michael Braungart 2002 book; biological and technical nutrient cycles eliminate waste.
EU Ecodesign Directive
Directive 2009/125/EC sets minimum efficiency for energy-related products; banned filament bulbs in EU from 2012.
Eco-indicator 99
Pre 1999 single-score LCA method aggregating ecosystem quality, human health and resources damage; updated to ReCiPe 2008.
Embodied energy
Total energy used to produce a material; aluminium ~155 MJ/kg, steel ~30 MJ/kg, glass ~15 MJ/kg, virgin polymers ~80 MJ/kg.
Life Cycle Assessment
ISO 14040 (2006) standardises cradle-to-grave impact assessment; covers extraction, manufacture, transport, use, disposal.
Six Rs framework
Reduce, refuse, reuse, repair, recycle, rethink; design strategy for circular economy adoption.
Accessibility standards
WCAG 2.1 (W3C 2018) for digital; ADA 1990 US physical; ISO 21542 (2011) built environment guidance.
Empathy mapping
Dave Gray XPLANE 2005 visualises user thinks, says, feels, does; complements IDEO's Field Guide to Human-Centered Design 2015.
Inclusive design
Microsoft Inclusive Design Toolkit 2016 by Kat Holmes; solve for one, extend to many; permanent, temporary, situational disabilities.
Journey mapping
Visualises user touchpoints across time; identifies pain points and opportunities; service blueprint adds backstage processes.
Personas
Alan Cooper's About Face 1995 popularised personas; fictional users encode research; primary, secondary, anti-personas.
User-centred design
Donald Norman 1986 framed UCD in User Centered System Design; ISO 9241-210 (2010) sets standard process.
